Fagin. The calculating criminal mastermind who directs a gang of child pickpockets from a squalid London hideout in Oliver Twist. He operates a school of pickpockets, training orphaned children to steal handkerchiefs, watches, and purses from unsuspecting Londoners. These pupils return their stolen goods to a dilapidated house where he lodges them, paying them in scraps of food and false camaraderie. He calls himself the Artful Dodger's master and rules through a mixture of paternal affection and calculated fear, welcoming new recruits with the iconic phrase, "You are made a member of the gang, old boy," though they become his victims rather than his partners. When cornered by magistrates and the law, he attempts to save himself by betraying his own gang, but is ultimately captured and hanged. His characterization is marked by Dickens' use of stereotypical Jewish traits, though the novel ultimately condemns the system that produced him as much as his crimes. As a Jewish criminal of legendary cunning, he exploits orphans' vulnerability and hunger to steal, then shields himself behind them when the law closes in.
